channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Molly Webster becomes a co-host of Radiolab
item.description: Longtime producer Molly Webster will join Latif Nasser as co-host of Radiolab, succeeding Lulu Miller as the public-radio show approaches its 25th anniversary. Webster has worked on the program since 2012 and created its Gonads and Breathe series. Miller will concentrate on the family-oriented spinoff Terrestrials.

item.title: Indonesia considers making platforms pay for news aggregation
item.description: A proposed Indonesian copyright bill would require large platforms to compensate publishers when aggregating news or displaying previews and snippets. With more than 230 million internet users, Indonesia could become Southeast Asia’s first country with such a regime. Critics question the state-run payment system and permit sanctions.

item.title: iHeart denies a report that it plans to sell its podcast division
item.description: Bloomberg reported that iHeartMedia was exploring a sale of part or all of its podcast operation, but the company said it has no such plan. The division produced $174 million in third-quarter revenue, up 24.6 percent. CEO Bob Pittman says iHeart will begin reporting podcast results separately so investors can better see the unit’s value.

item.title: A personal blog can serve its writer before it serves an audience
item.description: Bob Dunn argues that a blog need not chase reach or polish every entry into an essay. Quick thoughts, links and photos can build a durable personal archive on a site the writer controls, creating value even when nobody else reads a post. It is a crisp case for publishing on your own domain.

item.title: Former Ringer producers launch a podcast about how the web used to feel
item.description: Bobby Wagner and Alex Bazeley’s independent Click Through turns Wikipedia racing into a weekly show: start at two unrelated pages and navigate between them using only links. Recorded around New York, it treats Wikipedia, websites and digressive browsing as an antidote to platform-controlled discovery.

item.title: WordCamp Asia 2027 heads to Penang with a $35 ticket
item.description: The WordPress community will gather April 9–11 at Penang’s waterfront convention center for Contributor Day and two conference days. The 2026 edition drew 2,627 people and more than 1,500 contributors; registration for the 2027 Contributor Day opens Jan. 27 and is capped at 600.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 Beta 5 resolves known PHP 8.6 compatibility issues
item.description: The final beta before release candidates adds security, accessibility and compatibility fixes, including application-password notifications and better keyboard navigation. WordPress says all known core conflicts with PHP 8.6 are resolved, though plugin and theme testing remains essential before the Dec. 8 release.

item.title: Message Heard enters liquidation after cutting staff and freelancers
item.description: Podnews reports that the UK podcast producer has made staff redundant, ended 14 freelance contracts and entered voluntary liquidation. Multiple contributors say they are owed money, while the company’s history show Conflicted stopped publishing in October without a formal finale.

item.title: Remote local newsrooms save rent but lose institutional memory
item.description: A Northwestern Local News Initiative report examines what vanishes when publications give up shared offices: informal training, collaboration and knowledge passed between generations. Nieman Lab lists more than a dozen U.S. papers that have gone remote or sharply downsized since 2020.

item.title: WriteFreely patches critical authentication and federation flaws
item.description: WriteFreely 0.17.3 fixes an authentication bypass that could let an unauthenticated attacker use the API as another user. The open-source blogging release also closes private-content exposure through ActivityPub, a WebFinger request flaw and several access-control problems; administrators are urged to update.

item.title: WordPress Credits passes 50 participating institutions
item.description: More than 50 colleges and universities across 17 countries now award academic recognition for contributing to WordPress. The free program pairs students with mentors on translation, documentation, learning materials, development and testing; its dashboard counted 364 graduates by Oct. 19.

item.title: Spreaker pledges safeguards against unauthorized podcast copies
item.description: After Podnews documented copied shows on Spreaker, the Triton Digital platform committed to changes aimed at stopping unauthorized imports and protecting creators. The development turns scrutiny of podcast copying into a concrete response and renewed attention to feed ownership.

item.title: RSS.com expands video podcasting through open feed enclosures
item.description: RSS.com says its HLS video service now carries video through Apple Podcasts and supporting Podcasting 2.0 apps while preserving audio playback elsewhere. Video is placed in the RSS feed as an alternate enclosure, with supported apps including Pocket Casts, Fountain, TrueFans and Podcast Guru.

item.title: Transistor keeps podcast feeds readable without XSLT
item.description: Transistor rebuilt the browser presentation of its podcast RSS feeds with CSS ahead of Chrome's planned removal of XSLT. The new view retains cover art, show information, the feed URL and episode listings, offering a practical way for human-readable feeds to survive a browser-platform change.

item.title: Salon ceases publication after 31 years on the web
item.description: Salon has stopped publishing after a 31-year run that began when original online journalism was still an experiment. The publication said the economics of independent digital media made its model unsustainable, closing a site whose politics, culture, criticism and essays helped define web-native magazines.
